rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gates of Hell are the seven gates mentioned elsewhere.
rows.anchor: The reference is to the seven gates of Hell explained at another instance.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condemned are told to enter Hell, remain there forever, and expect no escape.
rows.anchor: Enter them and now you shall have to stay here forever and never expect that you will get out of here.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat reassures the Prophet to be patient: punishment will come in his lifetime or, otherwise, after his return to God.
rows.anchor: These words sound an assurance to the Prophet (sws) that he should show patience on the misdeeds of his opponents.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Messengers warned of worldly punishment for rejection and of Hereafter punishment; the threat here refers to the worldly punishment, which is part of the Hereafter punishment in essence.
rows.anchor: the words h refer to the first of these punishments because with reference to its essence it is part of the punishment of the Hereafter

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muḥammad’s community was threatened with worldly punishment, but most accepted faith, so it was spared; the troublemakers’ case was deferred to the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: the majority embraced faith; hence no such punishment visited them as visited the rejecters of the previous messengers

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rejecters customarily taunted messengers by demanding that they show a sample of the threatened punishment.
rows.anchor: to pester the messenger their addressees asked their messenger to show them a sample of this punishment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: History shows messengers cannot produce punishment signs on demand; whether such a sign comes depends on God’s wisdom.
rows.anchor: the history of the messengers of God bears witness that a messenger does not have the authority to show such signs

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should not demand such a sign and the Prophet should not fret over the demand; when God’s decree arrives, justice falls on those who deny the truth and reject messengers.
rows.anchor: when the decree of God is delivered complete justice is done and at that time those people are taken to task

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After consigning the demanded punishment sign to God, the passage turns the challengers to the many signs of providence around them.
rows.anchor: In this verse, attention of those who were demanding a sign of punishment is directed to the signs of God’s providence

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made livestock useful for transport, food, and other needs; camels served Arabs as desert ships, while animals and ships enabled travel and plans.
rows.anchor: some of which are useful to them as a means of transport; some others are useful in providing food to them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such provision is enough evidence of God’s providence and accountability; the demand for a punishment sign is an excuse, since signs abound but people fail to see them.
rows.anchor: are these not enough signs of God. How many of the signs will they deny?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier peoples were more numerous, powerful, and accomplished in construction, yet their amassed achievements could not protect them from God’s punishment.
rows.anchor: It is a reference to he architectural feats of the ‘ Ād and the Thamūd that have been alluded to at other places of the Qur’ ān.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: آثارا points to the architectural achievements of the ʿĀd and Thamūd.
rows.anchor: It is a reference to he architectural feats of the ‘ Ād and the Thamūd that have been alluded to at other places of the Qur’ ān.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A morally decadent nation cannot survive merely through population size or achievements that mark its culture and civilization.
rows.anchor: when a nation falls into moral decadence, then it cannot survive merely

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When messengers brought clear signs of monotheism, the Hereafter, and recompense, their people exalted meager knowledge, mocked the warning, and were enveloped by the punishment.
rows.anchor: because of their meanness they regarded their meager knowledge to be great and reckoned that whatever they see from their eyes is all that exists

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arguments had not brought faith, but upon seeing punishment the people professed belief in the one God and rejected their other deities; that late faith did not benefit them.
rows.anchor: their faith was of no avail to them when they saw Our punishment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only faith adopted through reasoning before punishment arrives is accepted; faith once punishment looms is useless, and the punishment routes its targets.
rows.anchor: Only that faith is acceptable to God which is embraced on the basis of reasoning before the punishment visits them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is God’s established practice: those who reject Him when punishment arrives are ruined and humiliated.
rows.anchor: When the punishment arrives, then those who reject it at that time are definitely ruined and humiliated.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The section extends its earlier monotheism discussion: God alone accomplishes, gives sustenance and offspring, and the universe’s harmony shows that no other will can interfere.
rows.anchor: except for the will and intention of the one and only God, there is no other will or intention that can interfere in it.

words: أَنْ أَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلدِّينَ وَلَا تَتَفَرَّقُوا۟ فِيهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same monotheistic religion was preached from Noah through Jesus and Muḥammad, with the command to uphold it without division.
rows.anchor: from Noah (sws) to Jesus (sws) every prophet has preached this very religion of monotheism and stopped people from creating differences in it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Followers divided the religion after receiving clear knowledge and thereby deprived themselves of God’s guidance.
rows.anchor: their followers created differences in it even after they had been given clear knowledge and thereby deprived themselves of God’s guidance.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is directed to invite people to this prophetic religion and adhere firmly to its call.
rows.anchor: the Prophet Mu ḥammad (sws) is directed to preach this very religion of the prophets before people and should strongly adhere to its call.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He is to tell opponents that he believes in God’s revealed Book, sent to judge the differences they created.
rows.anchor: he has professed faith in the Book of God which He has revealed to judge between the differences they have created

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If opponents reject the Book’s judgment, the Final Day’s scale will decide between them; the Day of Judgment is certain.
rows.anchor: if they do not accept its judgement, then the scale set up on Final Day will judge between them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Present affluence does not prove people are rightly guided: God gives worldly riches even to truth’s enemies, who will have no share in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: the Almighty gives affluence and riches in this world to those also who are the enemies of the truth; however, they will have no share in the Hereafter.
